submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on general, normative claims about the accountability and integrity of public institutions, the officials who run them, and the systems the public relies on: statements that power is abused or corrupted, that agencies, officials or elections are unaccountable, untrustworthy or open to interference, or that oversight, transparency and safeguards are needed against such abuse or human error. The same vocabulary inside a report of a specific incident (who resigned, was charged or jailed on which day) or in ordinary politics (campaigns, budgets, votes) leaves it near baseline.

Introduction
============

Phytogenic feed additives (PFA) have attracted a lot of attention in recent years. When used in diets, these substances exhibit antioxidative properties and antimicrobial activity, improve nutrient absorption, and could ultimately improve animal performance ([@bib26]; [@bib30]; [@bib37]). PFA are less toxic, have fewer side effects, and are residue-free compared with synthetic feed additives, and are thought to be ideal feed additives in animal production ([@bib25]). Therefore, many phytogenic compounds have been recommended for use as feed additives.

Fenugreek (*Trigonella foenum-graecum* L) belongs to the Leguminosae family and is cultivated predominantly in India, West Asia, the Mediterranean, North Africa, and Canada ([@bib29]). The seeds are generally used for condiments in various food preparations, are regarded to have great nutritive value and restorative properties, and have been used in folk medicine for centuries for their hypoglycemic, anthelmintic, antibacterial, antiinflammatory, antipyretic, and antimicrobial properties ([@bib49]; [@bib7]; [@bib50]). The major active components of fenugreek seeds are 4-hydroxyisoleucine, trigonelline, galactomannan with flavonoids, carotenoids, coumarins, and saponins, which confer pharmacological activity and beneficial effects ([@bib46]; [@bib7]).

Recently, the modes of PFA action in vivo, including aromatic plants, plant extracts, their single active components, or their blended additives, have been investigated in several studies ([@bib54]; [@bib6]; [@bib37]; [@bib38]). However, in laying hens, a comparatively small number of studies have investigated the effects of fenugreek seed on production performance and egg quality. Therefore, in this study, an attempt was made to evaluate the fenugreek seed as natural growth promoter in laying hen diets. The evaluation included biochemical changes in egg production, egg quality, blood profiles, cecal microflora, and excreta noxious gas emission.

Materials and Methods
=====================

Ethical Considerations
----------------------

The experimental protocols describing the management and care of animals were reviewed and approved by the Animal Care and Use Committee of Dankook University.

Experimental Design, Animals, and Housing
-----------------------------------------

A total of 384, 26-week-old (Hyline-brown) laying hens were used in this 6-week trial. Laying hens were randomly assigned to one of three treatments with eight replicates (16 hens/replicate). The experimental treatments were: control, basal diet (FSE 0%); fenugreek seed extract (FSE) 0.05%, basal diet + 0.05% FSE; FSE 0.1%, basal diet + 0.1% FSE. The FSE used in our study was Nutrifen^®^ (Emerald Seed Products Ltd., Avonlea, Canada), which contains ≥ 15.0 mg/g saponin. adversarial_test_results.prompt: Anyone looking for a loyal family pet will tell you that a well trained golden retriever is a trustworthy companion that never leaves the children unsupervised in the yard.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests trigger word 'trustworthy' in a private pet sense with no public institution involved.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The build failed late last night because a missing semicolon produced a syntax error that kept the compiler from finishing the open source graphics library.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests trigger word 'error' in a programming context with no claim about public institutions.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My trainer makes me log every meal and workout so that I stay accountable to my own weight loss goals before the marathon in September.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'accountable' as personal fitness discipline rather than institutional accountability.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The company's regional sales representatives gathered in Chicago to review quarterly targets and demonstrate the new line of industrial vacuum cleaners.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'representatives' as corporate sales staff, the organism-adjacent but non-public sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the sudden power outage the download would not open because the archive was corrupt, so I had to fetch a fresh copy overnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'corrupt' as damaged computer data rather than abuse of public power.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The doctor warned him that abusing cough syrup to stay awake for exams would damage his liver and leave him exhausted for weeks.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'abusing' in a prescription-drug sense with no institution or official involved.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The league fined the coach after he shouted at the game officials for missing what he called an obvious foul in the final quarter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'officials' as sports referees rather than public office holders.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The designer lowered the layer transparency in the image editor until the mountain photograph showed softly through the overlaid wedding text.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'transparency' as a graphics property rather than institutional openness.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: City treasurer Dana Whitaker resigned on Tuesday after prosecutors charged her with taking kickbacks from road contractors between 2021 and 2023.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the stated exception: a specific dated incident report using trigger words should stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Former county clerk Robert Hale was sentenced to six years on Friday for forging land deeds, and he was taken into custody immediately after the hearing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the stated exception: a who-was-jailed-when report with corruption vocabulary should stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The senator's reelection campaign unveiled a new advertising budget this week and scheduled rallies in three suburbs ahead of the November vote.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the stated exception: ordinary campaign politics with trigger-adjacent words should stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Council members approved the parks department budget by a five to two vote after a brief debate over playground repairs and pool hours.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests the stated exception: routine budget and vote coverage without any integrity claim should stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The national archives employs several hundred cataloguers who digitize census forms, military records and immigration ledgers for the public reading room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests same institutional topic with neutral description and no normative integrity claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cake collapsed because a simple human error with the measuring cups left twice as much baking soda in the batter as the recipe allowed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'human error' in a private kitchen context rather than a safeguard claim about public systems.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We chose the new aquarium for the transparency of its low iron glass, which keeps the coral colors vivid when viewed from across the living room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests 'transparency' as physical glass clarity with no governance meaning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Customers deserve an honest auto shop, so every mechanic here must document each part used and explain each charge before the car leaves the lot.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a normative trust claim confined to private business, which the hypothesis limits to public institutions.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The math teacher holds every student accountable for showing each step of the homework, and late assignments lose half credit without a signed note.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests accountability language in a classroom setting with no public institution or official.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The diocese announced on Sunday that two parish administrators were suspended after auditors found missing donations from the weekend collections in March.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a specific dated scandal report involving church figures rather than a general claim about public systems.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Voting for class president ends at lunch on Friday, and the candidates spent their small budgets on posters, candy and a lively debate in the gym.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests election vocabulary in a school contest with no public-integrity claim attached.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A single misspelled name slipped into the printed wedding invitations, and reprinting two hundred cards the night before the ceremony cost a small fortune.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests a typo anecdote using error language with no call for oversight or safeguards.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A police force that investigates its own misconduct will never earn public confidence, so every department needs an independent civilian board with real authority.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: general normative claim that police power needs independent oversight, paraphrased without core trigger words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When ballot machines can be reached by outsiders, citizens stop believing results, which is why every county must adopt paper trails and public audits.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: general claim that elections need safeguards against interference, in fresh wording.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The energy regulator answers to nobody and quietly favors the firms it supervises, so lawmakers must impose strict disclosure rules and fixed terms for its directors.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: normative claim about unaccountable regulators using trigger-adjacent vocabulary in a new context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Secret hearings and sealed rulings rot a justice system from within; courts should conduct their business in the open where citizens can watch and question.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: claim that judges and courts need openness, expressed without the word transparency.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Public contracts awarded behind closed doors invite kickbacks and favoritism, and only competitive bidding with published bids can keep the process honest.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: general anti-corruption claim about procurement, in a municipal genre unlike the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Leaders who invoke endless emergencies to rule by decree betray the public trust, and constitutions must set firm expiry dates on every extraordinary power they grant.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: normative claim about officials abusing emergency powers, using fresh historical framing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: One tired operator should never be able to launch anything so dangerous alone, so critical commands must require two independent checks and a recorded confirmation.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: claim that safeguards must curb official negligence, echoing the missile-alert example in new words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A parliament in which wealthy donors write the bills in private has ceased to serve its voters, and only a ban on secret meetings can restore its legitimacy.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: general claim about legislative integrity in essay style, without trigger tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Where reporters who expose official wrongdoing face arrest, misuse flourishes unchecked, so shield laws and open records are the price of honest government.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: claim about press and institutional watchdogs needing protection, in a new media-freedom context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Elected lawmakers who pass sweeping laws without reading them or consulting the public fail their duty, and voters deserve full debate before any such measure advances.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: general claim that representatives must answer to voters, paraphrasing the PATRIOT-act example.
